neighbours.label: the particle of a verb for stepping forward into a public role or performance (get up to speak, step in, go out on stage)
fire: When his name was called, the nervous student got up and walked to the podium.
Two elderly guests got up to dance in the middle of the hall.
Contestants must get up on stage and answer the judges' questions.
When the captain was injured, a rookie stepped in and led the team.
The band went out to a roaring crowd for the encore.
Our seniors want to go out on a high note tonight, the coach said.
The deputy stepped up to give the speech in her place.
After the applause, the comedian came out for one more bow.
quiet: When his name was called, the nervous student answered quietly from his seat.
Two elderly guests sat chatting in the middle of the hall.
Contestants must write their answers and hand them to the judges.
When the captain was injured, the team lost three games in a row.
The band packed their gear after the long show.
Our seniors played very well tonight, the coach said.
The deputy wrote the speech for her the night before.
After the applause, the comedian thanked the staff backstage.
